name: quotient_filter
description:
Aggregate that builds a Quotient filter. Three forms:

- `quotient_filter(q, r, value)` — `q` quotient bits (the filter holds at most 2^q − 1 values; one slot always stays empty) and `r` remainder bits per slot (false positive rate ~2^−r). `q + r` must be at most 64. Inserting more than 2^q − 1 distinct values raises `the filter is full`.
- `quotient_filter(r, value)` — self-sizing: collects the values and picks `q` so the distinct values fill at most 3/4 of the 2^q slots. No need to guess `q`.
- `quotient_filter(q, r, filter)` — merges Quotient filter BLOBs into one filter with exactly the given `q` and `r`. Each input must have `q_in + r_in >= q + r`, since a filter only keeps `q + r` bits of each hash — so a merge can grow `q` only by giving up as many remainder bits (merge `(16, 8)` filters into `(20, 4)`, not `(20, 8)`). Inputs must be built from the same value type; overflowing the merged filter is an error.

Accepts values of any type: `UBIGINT` values are used as 64-bit keys exactly as given; every other type is hashed with XXH64 of a fixed encoding that does not change between DuckDB versions.

examples.description: Build a Quotient filter per partition
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE filters AS
SELECT id % 2 AS remainder,
       quotient_filter(16, 8, id) AS filter
FROM series_data
GROUP BY id % 2;

examples.description: Let the filter size itself (~0.4% FPR)
examples.code: SELECT quotient_filter(8, id) AS filter FROM ids;
SELECT quotient_filter(16, 8, filter) AS merged FROM filters;

name: quotient_filter_contains
description: Test whether a value is a member of a Quotient filter. Returns BOOLEAN — false means definitely-not-present; true means probably-present (within the filter's configured false-positive rate). The probe value is cast to the type the filter was built from, so `42` and `'42'` both work against a `BIGINT` filter; a value that cannot be cast (e.g. `'abc'` against an integer filter) returns false, and a NULL probe returns NULL.

examples.description: Membership test against a stored filter
examples.code:
SELECT quotient_filter_contains(filter, 12345) AS might_exist
FROM filters WHERE remainder = 1;

name: xor8_filter
description: Aggregate that builds an 8-bit XOR filter. ~9 bits per key, ~0.39% false positive rate. Static — built once, queried many times. ~20% smaller than Bloom for the same FPR. Accepts values of any type: `UBIGINT` values are used as 64-bit keys exactly as given; every other type is hashed with XXH64 of a fixed encoding that does not change between DuckDB versions.

examples.description: Build an xor8 filter from a column
examples.code: SELECT xor8_filter(id) AS filter FROM ids;

name: xor16_filter
description: Aggregate that builds a 16-bit XOR filter. ~18 bits per key, ~0.0015% false positive rate. Use when you need a much lower FPR than xor8 and can afford 2× the memory. Accepts values of any type: `UBIGINT` values are used as 64-bit keys exactly as given; every other type is hashed with XXH64 of a fixed encoding that does not change between DuckDB versions.

examples.description: Build an xor16 filter for low FPR
examples.code: SELECT xor16_filter(id) AS filter FROM ids;

name: binary_fuse8_filter
description: Aggregate that builds an 8-bit Binary Fuse filter. The most space-efficient filter family — typically <9 bits per key — with very fast construction and lookups. Static structure. Accepts values of any type: `UBIGINT` values are used as 64-bit keys exactly as given; every other type is hashed with XXH64 of a fixed encoding that does not change between DuckDB versions.

examples.code: SELECT binary_fuse8_filter(id) AS filter FROM ids;

name: bloom_filter

parameters.name: ndv
parameters.description: Expected number of distinct values. Must be a positive constant.

parameters.name: fpp
parameters.description: Target false positive rate, between 0 and 1. Must be a constant.

description: Aggregate that builds a split block Bloom filter — the Parquet Bloom filter format — sized for `ndv` distinct values at false positive rate `fpp`. Sizing uses the same formula as DuckDB's Parquet writer, rounded up to a power of two of 32-byte blocks (at most 2 GB). For the same values and sizing the result is byte-for-byte the filter DuckDB writes into Parquet files. Values of any type are hashed with XXH64 of their Parquet plain encoding — unlike the other filters, `UBIGINT` values are hashed too, for Parquet compatibility. A Bloom filter never gets "full": insert more than `ndv` values and the false positive rate degrades gradually.

examples.description: Bloom filter for ~1,000 keys at 1% FPR
examples.code: SELECT bloom_filter(1000, 0.01, key) AS filter FROM keys;

name: bloom_filter_merge
description: Aggregate that merges Bloom filters into one filter containing every value of the inputs (a bitwise OR). All inputs must be built with the same `ndv` and `fpp` and from the same value type; otherwise it raises an error. The union of per-group filters is exactly the filter of all the values.

examples.description: Roll per-bucket filters up into one
examples.code: SELECT bloom_filter_merge(bf) AS filter FROM bucket_blooms;

name: bloom_filter_contains
description: Test whether a value might be a member of a Bloom filter built by `bloom_filter` or `bloom_filter_merge`. False means definitely-not-present; true means probably-present. The probe value is cast to the type the filter was built from, so `42` and `'42'` both work against a `BIGINT` filter; a value that cannot be cast (e.g. `'abc'` against an integer filter) returns false, and a NULL probe returns NULL.

name: bitfilter_contains
description: Test whether any bitfilters filter may contain a value. The filter's header says what kind of filter it is and how its values were hashed, so one function probes Quotient, XOR, Binary Fuse and Bloom filters alike. Requires a BLOB with a header — filters written by older versions of the extension must be probed with their type-specific `*_contains` function. The probe value is cast to the type the filter was built from, so `42` and `'42'` both work against a `BIGINT` filter; a value that cannot be cast (e.g. `'abc'` against an integer filter) returns false, and a NULL probe returns NULL.

examples.description: Probe a column holding mixed filter types

name: bitfilter_info

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter BLOB with a bitfilters header.

returns: A STRUCT with `filter_type`, `format_version`, `key_hash` (`'none'` or `'xxhash64'`), `key_type`, `size_bytes`, `entries`, `capacity`, `load_factor`, `fingerprint_bits`, `bits_per_entry`, `expected_fpr`, `q`, `r` and `seed`. Fields a filter type doesn't have are NULL.
description: Describe any bitfilters filter BLOB: what kind of filter it is, how its values became keys, its size and its expected false positive rate. Requires a header; use the type-specific `*_info` function for BLOBs written by older versions.

name: bitfilter_is_valid
description: Return whether a BLOB is a structurally valid bitfilters filter with a header, instead of raising the error a probe would. BLOBs written by older versions (no header) return false here; check them with the type-specific `*_is_valid` function.

examples.description: Find BLOBs that aren't valid filters
examples.code: SELECT * FROM filters WHERE NOT bitfilter_is_valid(filter);

name: bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_create
description: Build a Bloom filter compatible with DuckDB's internal join filter format. Produced filters can be used in custom join optimization paths and in zone-map-style data skipping. The first argument is the DuckDB version whose filter layout to produce (`v1.4.0` through `v2.0`).

name: bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_probe
description: Test whether a hash value might be a member of a DuckDB-compatible Bloom filter built by `bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_create`. The version must be constant. The filter can be a constant BLOB (parsed once at bind time), a scalar subquery, or a per-row BLOB column (read per row), so one query can probe a different filter on each row. A `NULL` filter returns `NULL`. Extra value arguments are combined for multi-key filters.

name: bitfilters_duckdb_hash
description: Hash function compatible with DuckDB's internal Bloom filter probe layout. Use this rather than a generic hash when feeding values into the DuckDB-style Bloom filter functions. The first argument is a constant DuckDB version string — `v1.4.0`–`v1.4.4`, `v1.5.0`, `v1.5.1`, `v1.6.0` or `v2.0` — and the result equals that version's built-in `hash()`; extra value arguments are combined the way `hash(a, b, ...)` combines them.
